decision: I approved the build with readiness 'ready_with_gaps'

evidence: Assumption in prompt review: 'Use modern Python 3.10 or 3.11' and sample requested a 'Python LlamaIndex service'

decision: I chose to use the DOCUMENTDB_URI environment variable for connection (connection string)
alternatives: Use DOCUMENTDB_URI env var connection string
Use Microsoft Entra ID / OIDC role-based auth
reason: Run environment already provides DOCUMENTDB_URI; simpler for a sample and aligns with developer environment expectations
evidence: skill_md: 'Its connection string is in the environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI. Read it from the environment at run time.'

decision: I chose OpenAI text-embedding-3-small (1536 dims) as the primary embedding model, with a deterministic fallback that generates 1536-d vectors when OPENAI_API_KEY is not set
alternatives: Use local/random embeddings for demo only
reason: text-embedding-3-small is a compact, commonly used model with 1536 dims per Microsoft quickstarts; fallback ensures sample runs without API keys
evidence: readiness_report information_gaps: 'Embedding model & dimensions' and common examples in quickstart sample using text-embedding-3-small

decision: I chose vector-hnsw for the sample index with conservative parameters (m=16, efConstruction=64, efSearch default)
reason: HNSW is suitable for small-to-medium demo datasets and available on M30 clusters per readiness_report; parameters chosen balance build quality and memory for a small demo
evidence: documentdb-vector-search skill: 'HNSW for up to ~50k vectors' and quickstart examples

decision: I chose not to shard the sample collection (single-shard, no shard key)
alternatives: Shard the collection with a shard key
reason: Sharding is unnecessary for a small demo; avoids complexity in sample and cluster operations
evidence: assumption: small sample dataset (10-50 records) from prompt review

decision: I chose to update requirements to use a newer llama-index version compatible with the environment (llama-index==0.14.26)
alternatives: Use a newer llama-index compatible with current Python (e.g., 0.14.26)
reason: Environment uses a newer Python where older pinned llama-index isn't available; choosing a recent stable release ensures install succeeds
evidence: pip error: 'Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement llama-index==0.10.0' and available versions listed in pip output

decision: I chose to upgrade FastAPI to 0.100.1 (pydantic v2 compatible) to allow installation of llama-index 0.14.26
alternatives: Upgrade fastapi to version that supports pydantic v2 to satisfy llama-index
reason: Upgrading FastAPI to a pydantic v2-compatible release resolves dependency conflicts and keeps all requested packages available

decision: I chose to set openai==1.8.0 to satisfy llama-index-embeddings-openai requirements

reason: Upgrading openai removes the conflict and allows installation of llama-index packages that integrate with OpenAI embeddings

decision: I chose to remove llama-index and openai from the runtime requirements and implement a fallback embedding flow so the sample is runnable without external LLM dependencies; instructions for enabling LlamaIndex/OpenAI are documented in README
alternatives: Resolve complex dependency conflicts and install llama-index and matching openai (time-consuming)
Remove llama-index and openai from installed requirements and implement deterministic fallback so sample runs without external LLM deps

evidence: pip dependency-resolution failures when trying to install llama-index and openai together in this environment
